sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 2 = check 1; Internal Quality Checks row 2; no cell comments on either)
evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md (5 lines, 683 bytes) is three short first-person prose paragraphs. Line 1 gives a motive and a personal workflow: "I'd like a small local playground for working on JavaScript and complete HTML files. The editor itself matters: I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source. I want to keep the versions that work without losing a draft when another tab saves first." Line 3 points at the notes ("Please read the six notes in /instructions before building"); exactly six notes exist (behaviour, integration, overview, policy, security, ui) and environment/Dockerfile:14-15 copies /instructions and /assets. Line 5 states where to put the app and the no-sign-in outcome. None of the skill's check-1 defect markers (quality-checks.md:11) is present in instruction.md: no numbered acceptance list, no bullets, no shall/must table, no feature matrix, no framework, file layout or endpoint list. The template's CHANGE_ME placeholder has been replaced. The notes stay in prose paragraphs under plain headings and keep the first person (ui.md:3 "the source I see", behaviour.md:11 "must not touch what I am doing", integration.md:1 "How we start the app"); the runtime facts (node /app/server.js, 0.0.0.0:3000, GET /api/health, SQLite, DB_PATH) sit in integration.md:3-9, where check 4 requires them, and policy.md:3 leaves layout, labels, routes and schema to the builder, so it is not a build recipe. Observation, not a defect under this row: ui.md (9 paragraphs, 4574 bytes) and behaviour.md are dense with must/must-not sentences and enumerated editor behaviours and read closer to a requirements note than casual speech; that density is prose rather than a checklist or table, is needed for check 4/6 fairness, and the voice question belongs to row 2. This row is a reading judgement on static text; no runtime measurement is required for it, and none is claimed.
